experiments.scope: Complete 41-round SHA-256 on the 64-byte two-block W[0..7]-prefix message family; bounded merging distinguished-point birthday walk embedded on the low 16 bits of the final 2-block digest (256 organizer trials, strict total budget max 285 evaluations/trial including both Pass-1 search and Pass-2 recovery, dp_bits=2), plus deterministic self-test emitting and executing the complete 4-byte body (45,312 records) and 5-byte native VM image (1,433-record 8x-unrolled zero-stub outer controller + 1,238-record unrolled 2-lane SIMD RecProg) with 256/256 verification against complete 41-round SHA-256 and a direct 64-trial w=12 iterated Walk-B F(Y) birthday check.
experiments.hypothesis: The bounded merging distinguished-point birthday search on the 64-byte W[0..7]-prefix 2-block digest map recovers distinct message pairs colliding on the low 16 bits of complete 41-round SHA-256 at the random-function DP birthday rate (~40-43%) within the strict 285-evaluation total budget, while selftest() verifies both single-step Walk-B equivalence (256/256) and direct iterated Walk-B F(Y) birthday behavior at w=12.

experiments.scope: Complete 41-round SHA-256 on the 64-byte two-block W[0..7]-prefix message family; fixed-budget birthday collision projection at width w=14 bits (256 organizer trials, budget M=127 evaluations/trial, exact discrete random-function collision probability 0.387131).
experiments.hypothesis: Under H1, the empirical collision frequency on the low 14 bits of complete 41-round SHA-256 across 256 independent trials at budget M=127 matches the random-function birthday prediction of approximately 0.39.
